A register of needs every system has (privacy, security contact, accessibility, email authentication, entity, backups, succession, renewals, tax) is probed against the repository; gaps become executor items, identity-bound ones become gates, and recurring domain sweeps keep asking what nobody thought to ask.
managers.trigger: every executor or cloud-session pass (blindspots --scan --apply) and on each new incident, reply or finding (blindspots --learn)

managers.summary: UNKNOWNS-1: what the system does not know is a core feedback loop. Every loop and blind-spot need is questioned through inverted lenses (pre-mortem, assumption audit, red team, Rumsfeld blind side, UIA protected and scaffold ignorance), scored, and filed as plus items; answers with evidence record a gap or new objective, which becomes a probationary objective candidate and seeds the next pass, so the solution space keeps expanding instead of shrinking around what is known.
managers.trigger: every executor or cloud-session pass (unknowns --run --apply), weekly per question; on each answer (unknowns --answer)

managers.summary: k_eff is acted on, not only measured: after three subcritical beats the tick Worker's dispatch lever moves to raise-only, the move carries the prediction 'k_eff > k within 24 h', a miss reverts it and files CRIT-LEVER, a stall files CRIT-STALL; one criticality_history row per tick is the loop's clock.
managers.trigger: every tick (cron */10 on the tick Worker)

managers.summary: Ashby's second loop: every tick reads each essential variable against its bounds; one out of bounds for two ticks takes one discrete step (a parameter change within limits, or a restructure item), kept only if the variable returns, otherwise undone and the next step taken; an exhausted ladder files a redesign item.
managers.trigger: daily cost-guard workflow and the criticality tick

managers.summary: No remote branch carries work main lacks. Every branch gets one recorded disposition (merged, superseded, ported as a PORT-BRANCH item, rejected on purpose, or state): generated-file conflicts resolve by rule, a merge that breaks the gate is undone, merged branches are pruned. Closes the blind spot of the session reaper, which only watched agent/ and claude/ branches.
managers.trigger: daily workflow and every lane run

managers.summary: LOOPPROOF-1: the proof that every server-side loop ran every time. Each loop of the scheduled handler runs inside beat(), which writes a row before the loop starts and its result or error after; the tick step pulse counts expected against good slots over 24 h per loop and for the tick itself, writes loop_clock, files MISSED-<loop> for a loop that is late, stopped, failing, hung or never ran, and closes it when the loop ticks again. The site Worker (hourly) and the dashboard Worker (*/10) are the second producers: each calls /pulse/watch and the tick Worker runs a tick itself when the newest one is stale.
managers.trigger: every tick (cron */10 on ultrastable-tick), the dashboard Worker cron (*/10) and the site Worker cron (hourly) for the watchdog
managers.closing_probe: grep:seed/worker/test/pulse.test.js::a loop that stops is found, filed as MISSED-<loop>, and closed when it runs again

managers.summary: BOOT-KNOWS-1: the system reads, from its own tables, the stage it has reached from bootstrap to criticality (seeded, ticking, looping, closing, instrumented, critical, self-sustaining). The stage is the highest whose condition and every one below it hold; each change is appended to ignition_log with its evidence; the first unmet stage is IGNITE-<stage> with the numbers that block it, closed only by the same reading. bootstrapped is instrumented or above; critical needs k_eff at or above k_min for six ticks in a row.
managers.trigger: every tick, after the criticality step
managers.closing_probe: grep:seed/worker/test/pulse.test.js::ignition ladder: the stage is the highest whose condition and every one below it hold

managers.summary: Every public repository keeps LICENSE (canonical blob), NOTICE, COMMERCIAL-TERMS.md, CITATION.cff, SECURITY.md, no case-colliding paths, the SPDX header on new source (shrink-only baseline) and no personal email or local path. Cross-repo copies are drift-checked by fleet. Procedure of the pre-publication audit is data in doctrine/publication.json.
managers.trigger: every PR (checks.yml) and the daily fleet drift run

managers.summary: A11Y-LOOP-1: every public page is rendered at phone and desktop width, light and dark, and checked with axe-core, horizontal scroll and 44px targets; a failure files an issue.
managers.trigger: weekly (a11y.yml) and on demand

managers.summary: PROVENANCE-1: every input and change is a row with origin class, actor, channel, what it touched and its effect; the public changelog is redacted; settled effects feed the improvement ranker.
managers.trigger: every executor result, write-back and owner command; daily settle pass in product-manager.yml
managers.last_plus: settled outcomes retire or reinforce levers in selfimprove.provenance_candidates; the kept rate is printed by provenance --signal so the next run is comparable
managers.owns: the roadmap and the user value of one project.
each_tick: Turn the outcome into at most five roadmap items, each with goal, user, success metric.
Rank pluses proposed by staff and reviewers against the roadmap; accept the best into the reserved share.
Write acceptance criteria and a checkable prediction for each accepted item.
Read feedback and usage; file what changes the ranking.

managers.summary: The system watches every red X on its repositories' default branches: transient failures are rerun once, every other failure becomes a Q-CIFAIL queue item with its log tail and a closing probe, which the Actions-hosted code agent fixes; green runs are recorded too.
managers.trigger: daily, and a failed checks, lane, deploy or executor run

managers.summary: The system generates its own apps: ideates from its own records, scores reach and impact, gates safety, launches on *.ultrastable.app, and a portfolio manager scores measured value (verified gap closed, retention, reach to people with the gap) to keep, iterate, promote or retire each app.
managers.trigger: daily

managers.summary: Every claim on a public surface is a probed sentence, a block generated from code, or an inventory checked in reverse; drift fails the check, files a Q-CLAIM item and shows at /claims.
managers.trigger: every pull request (checks.yml) and daily workflow claims.yml

managers.summary: REPOS-1: the folded-in workers/ core is tested in Actions on every change under workers/.
managers.trigger: a pull request touching workers/ (workers-tests.yml) and on demand

managers.summary: Every open GitHub issue carries a probe; a passing probe closes the issue with its evidence, a failing one stays for the executor, a missing one is a defect (ISSUE-LOOP-1).
managers.trigger: daily workflow issueloop.yml

managers.summary: RESILIENCE-1: every clock keeps ticking. The watchdog probes every clock (doctrine/clocks.json and every scheduled workflow), restarts the stopped ones (workflow dispatch, or POST /pulse/watch on each Cloudflare account), escalates a restart that did not take as a Q-STALL item, and feeds the essential variable stalled_clocks. The GitHub watchdog and the tick Worker's watchdog loop restart each other.
managers.trigger: every 40 minutes from the tick Worker (watchdog-gh loop), daily and on every finished lane, deploy-site or executor run from GitHub Actions

managers.summary: Core is the system of record: every tenant pins workers/ by hash, never forks it, and every generic capability it builds is lifted into the core by a core PR; the core's changes flow back by re-vendor PRs. Backend only; each action is a ledger line.
managers.trigger: daily workflow and every push to workers/

managers.summary: Generated data (claims, dashboard, self-model, ultrastability, core contract, trigger register, plugin self-description) is regenerated by a bot after every merge to main, so pull requests stop racing each other to refresh it. PR checks still fail on real drift.
managers.trigger: push to main

managers.summary: HOSTS-1: one adapter interface (seed/worker/src/hosts.js) for Cloudflare, GitHub Actions and Google Cloud. Signed push webhooks deploy the touched workers through the first healthy host with failover; every deploy, failure and inbound host event (POST /hook/host) lands as a commit status or check run; the hosts loop probes each host's health and redispatches through the credential-free GitHub Actions host when a push has no deploy after 30 minutes. The host-hooks loop (hourly) derives the webhook secrets inside the Worker from CREDENTIAL_KEY and creates, repairs and re-checks the repository webhook itself through the GitHub App token; the site Worker forwards /hook/github and /hook/host to the tick. A token without hook rights is recorded plainly and the polling path stays.
managers.trigger: push webhooks on /hook/github (workflow_run is not subscribed: FREE-TIER-1), POST /hook/host, and every tick (loop 'hosts')
managers.closing_probe: grep:seed/worker/test/hosts.test.js::the reconciler creates a missing hook, repairs a failing one, and leaves a healthy one

managers.summary: The repository and every host that runs a system stay one state (HOSTSYNC-1): each verified deploy is recorded as expected, the host's live runtime state (module hash, binding names, cron schedules, workers.dev; never a secret value) is read through the deploy gateway and written back to ops/hosting/state.json, and a host that differs from the repository is redeployed. Backend only.
managers.trigger: after the deploy-gateway workflow, a host-changed callback, and a daily run

gaps.what: Issues, pull requests, review and CI run on GitHub. The tracker, the PR flow and the merge gate are not yet a system-owned forge.
gaps.plan: Define a forge adapter interface in seed/worker (list items, open change, record review, merge) with a git-local implementation that works on plain git plus docs/issues; GitHub becomes one adapter of it. Until then docs/issues is the system record and GitHub is a mirror.

gaps.what: Work is executed by coding agents started by people or sessions (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex). The worker queues dispatches but does not call a model itself (BS-4).
gaps.plan: Add seed/worker/src/executor.js with a provider interface (hosted model API, self-hosted model server, or a queue file a cloud-hosted agent drains) so any agent can take a dispatch; record each result as an outcome.

gaps.what: The owner receives reports and gives direction in Claude threads; the four-line report exists in the tick and /health but delivery is by thread.
gaps.plan: Closed by the communications plugin (seed/plugins/loops.py communications_tick): the four-line report is delivered to a configured address through the email plugin, behind the scope gate; dry-run until a reviewed PR sets mode live. Threads become one consumer.

gaps.what: Outreach and funding mail has no registered sender; queues are dry-run.
gaps.plan: Closed by seed/plugins/email (Cloudflare sender Worker template plus adapter) and mailing_list (double opt-in, unsubscribe, suppression), behind the consent and suppression gate. Live sending needs the owner to register one mailbox (identity-bound card, default: dry run).

gaps.what: Social posting depends on accounts a person must create.
gaps.plan: Adapters for Bluesky, Mastodon and Buffer exist in seed/plugins/social, text limited to the guard-approved self-description. Accounts are still created by a person; the adapters stay dry-run until a reviewed PR sets mode live.

gaps.what: Hosting, cron and D1 run on Cloudflare in production.
gaps.plan: Hosting is an adapter: the SQLite path boots the same tick on any host with Python (selfhost; CI runs it on every PR) and the GCP adapter carries the same core. Closed for the SQLite path; a live GCP deploy is tracked as a separate plus.

gaps.what: git is the only store of record; a machine without git cannot fetch the repo.
gaps.plan: Accepted: the repository is the system. The manual path accepts a zip of the repo, which selfhost boots identically.

gaps.what: The second runtime (Cloud Run with a SQLite volume) has tests but its live deploy script has never been run.
gaps.plan: Run platform/adapters/gcp/deploy.sh against a project once credits or a free tier exist and record the run in docs/handoff/gcp-live.md; until then the SQLite path proves portability.

gaps.what: A server-side scheduler has to call the recurring loop (a Cloudflare cron, a cloud-hosted Claude routine or a GitHub schedule). Until now the loops ran only when a person or session started them, and the cron worker ticked an empty seed-template database, not the real records.
gaps.plan: One command (python3 -m foundation launch) runs every loop and writes evidence to the repo; three server-side host adapters schedule it (Cloudflare cron worker loaded with the real records, cloud-hosted Claude routine, daily GitHub workflow gate). Closed when the command, registry, workflow and first evidence exist.

gaps.what: Starting the loops on a new Cloudflare account needed a token or connector re-authorization that a non-coder cannot supply; the loops had one host and one credential kind (failure record docs/failures/2026-11-11-single-route.md).
gaps.plan: Failover chain across server-side hosts (foundation/failover.py), a credential-free route on GitHub Actions' built-in token, server-side first-run routes (deploy/first-run/README.md: Deploy to Workers button, cloud session with the connector, the cf-account workflow), and a lint (scripts/check_routes.py). Closed when the live move to the new account runs through one of those routes.
